content:
Hi Folks. I'm finding the Zulip website quite confusing. Please let me know if this is a good or bad thing to post here. Or if there is another forum where it may be suitable.

I wanted to do some experiments with AI and mathematics since I heard the new Claude Fable was more capable than before.

I used Claude Code to produce a Lean formalisation of (a weakened version of) One of the Odd Zeta Values from ζ(5) to ζ(25) Is Irrational. By Elementary Means - Wadim Zudilin https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.09895 This includes formalisation of a theorem due to Hanson: d_n < 3^n which is the main ingredient missing from https://specfun.inria.fr/zeta-of-3/issac.pdf

I also tried to compute a recurrence relation for zeta(7) linear forms using the Holonomic Functions package https://risc.jku.at/sw/holonomicfunctions/ - I believe this succeeded, but the mathematics here is a fair bit above my level so I cannot verify this. This is not lean formalised and I want to move on from this experiment, but since I put a significant amount of computation into all of this there's a small chance its useful to somebody!

If you want the community to check the repository the best you can do is to ask Claude to set up comparator. The irrationality statement can be easily written using mathlib, so Challenge.lean should only import mathlib.

Also, it's a very good idea to provide a formalization.yaml file.
Thanks. I've run comparator and that passed. and I've created the formalization.yaml file also https://github.com/rain-1/odd-zeta-values-autoformalization/blob/main/zeta5odd/formalization.yaml
Add everything is needed for comparator to the repo, so we can see Challenge.lean.
Also, formalization.yaml should be in the root of the repo.
Sorry, I misunderstood the structure of the repository, my fault.
Can you use docs#riemannZeta in Challenge.lean? Also it's probably more readable if you use Odd j ∧ ... instead of Finset.filter (this is just cosmetic).
Note that there already is a full formalization that ζ 3 is irrational (I understand that your strategy is more elementary).

Ah interesting! There's probably a fair bit of overlap between these two repos even though they prove different theorems. And they prove a stronger lemma than Hanson's d_n < 3^n. This could strengthen the proof I have to work for the proper ζ(5) to ζ(25) list, I think.

I've made the improvements you suggested, switching to the proper libraries riemannZeta definition. Thank you!
